payload.passage: Show one painting to two groups, give each group a different title for it, and they will describe two different scenes. One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner. This happens because a title tells the eye where to begin. A viewer facing a new image has no order to follow, so the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame. Once that route is set, the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background. The same is true of a song or a story, since a name at the top decides what counts as the subject.

answer_key.rationale_ko: 글은 "a title tells the eye where to begin" 이라고 하고, 그 길이 정해지면 "the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background" 라고 마무리한다. 제목이 시선을 이끈다는 것이 요지다. 나머지는 소재만 같고 결론이 다르다 — ②는 이름을 붙이지 말자는 주장이라 글과 반대고, ③는 누가 이름을 정하느냐는 권리 문제로 글에 없다. ④는 색을 다루지만 글은 색이 아니라 말을 다루고, ⑤는 두 무리가 다르게 본 것을 근거로 쓰지만 그것은 예시일 뿐 주장이 아니다.

payload.passage: Show one painting to two groups, give each group a different title for it, and they will describe two different scenes. One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner. This happens because a title tells the eye where to begin. A viewer facing a new image has no order to follow, so the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame. Once that route is set, the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background. The same is true of a song or a story, since a name at the top decides what counts as the subject. For this reason a title is not a label stuck on after the work is done. It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision. Some artists refuse to name a piece at all, and that refusal is a choice too, because it hands the route back to the viewer.
payload.stem_ko: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

answer_key.rationale_ko: 같은 그림에 다른 제목을 주면 다른 장면을 보게 되는데, "a title tells the eye where to begin" 이기 때문이다. 나머지는 하늘이나 구석의 인물처럼 그 현상을 보여주려고 든 예시다.
